1.9: and Uzziah fathered Jotham, and Jotham fathered Ahaz, and Ahaz fathered Hezekiah,

5.1: Then they came to the other side of the sea, into the region of the Gadarenes.

5.13: Then immediately Jesus permitted them. And having come out, the unclean [ or, defiling ] spirits entered into the pigs, and the herd stampeded down the steep bank into the sea - now they were about two thousand - and they were being drowned in the sea.
5.14: So the ones feeding the pigs fled, and they reported [ it ] in the city and in the farms. And they came out to see what it is, the [ thing ] having happened.
5.15: And they come to Jesus, and they see the one being demon - possessed [ or, oppressed by demons ] sitting and having been clothed and being of sound mind, the one having had the legion. And they were frightened.

5.29: And immediately the flow of her blood was dried up, and she knew in her body that she has been healed of that affliction.

5.41: And having taken hold of the hand of the young child, He says to her, " Talitha koumi! " which is, being translated, " Girl ( I say to you ), get up! "
5.42: And immediately the girl rose up and was walking about! ( for she was twelve years [ old ] ). And they were amazed [ with ] great amazement.

6.1: Then He went out from there and came into His hometown, and His disciples follow Him.
6.2: And [ the ] Sabbath having come, He began to be teaching in the synagogue. And many hearing were astonished, saying, " Where [ did ] this One [ get ] these [ things ]? And what [ is ] the wisdom having been given to Him? And [ how ] are such miraculous works being done through His hands?
6.3: " This is the craftsman, the Son of Mary and Brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon, is it not? And His sisters are here with us, are they not? " And they were caused to stumble because of Him [ fig., were having doubts about Him ].

7.1: And the Pharisees and some of the scribes, having come from Jerusalem, are gathered together to Him.
7.2: And having seen some of His disciples eating bread with defiled [ or, ceremonially unclean ] hands - that is, not ritually washed - they found fault.
7.3: For the Pharisees and all the Jews, if they do not wash their hands with [ the ] fist [ fig., in the proper manner ], do not eat, keeping the tradition of the elders.
7.4: And [ coming ] from the marketplace, unless they baptize [ or, ceremonially wash ] themselves, they do not eat, and many other [ traditions there ] are which they received [ and ] are keeping: [ like ] baptisms [ or, ceremonial washings ] of cups and pitchers and brazen vessels and cots.
7.5: Afterwards the Pharisees and the scribes ask Him, " Why do Your disciples not walk about [ fig., conduct themselves ] according to the tradition of the elders? 9 But 9 they eat their bread with ritually unwashed hands. "

7.9: And He was saying to them, [ All too ] well do you * regard as nothing the commandment of God, so that you * should keep your * tradition.

7.11: " But 9 you * 9 say, 'If a person says to his father or to his mother, [ It is ] Corban ( which is, a gift ), whatever you should be benefited from me. " '

7.13: " [ thus ] nullifying the word of God for your * tradition which you * handed down. And many such other similar things you * do. "

7.22: thefts, covetous desires [ or, greed ], wicked deeds, deceit [ or, treachery ], flagrant sexual immorality, an evil eye [ fig., envy ], blasphemy, arrogance, foolishness.
7.23: " All these evils come out from within and defile the person. "

7.25: For a woman having heard about Him, whose little daughter was having an unclean [ or, defiling ] spirit, having come, she fell at His feet.
7.26: Now the woman was a Greek, a Syro - Phoenician by race. And she kept asking Him that He would cast out the demon from her daughter.
7.27: But Jesus said to her, " Allow the children to be filled first, for it is not proper to take the children's bread and to cast [ it ] to the little dogs. "
7.28: But she answered and says to Him, " Yes indeed, Lord, but even the little dogs under the table eat from the young children's crumbs. "
7.29: And He said to her, " Because of this word, be going; the demon has gone out from your daughter. "
7.30: And having gone away into her house, she found the demon having gone out and her daughter having been placed on the bed.
7.31: And again, having gone out from the borders of Tyre and Sidon, He came to the Sea of Galilee, in the middle of the borders of Decapolis [ or, Ten Cities ].

7.37: And they were utterly astonished, saying, " He has done all [ things ] well; He makes both the deaf to be hearing and the mute to be speaking! "

8.1: In those days, the crowd being very great and not having anything they should eat, Jesus having summoned His disciples, says to them,

8.28: So they answered, " John the Baptist [ or, the Immerser ], and others Elijah, but others one of the prophets. "
8.29: Then He says to them, " But you *, who do you * say Me to be [ or, [ that ] I am ]? " So answering, Peter says to Him, " 9 You 9 are the Christ " [ " the Anointed One " ].
8.30: And He warned them that they should be telling no one about Him.
8.31: Then He began to be teaching them that it is necessary [ for ] the Son of Humanity to suffer many [ things ] and to be rejected by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes and to be killed and after three days to rise again.
8.32: And He was speaking the word plainly. And Peter, having taken Him aside, began rebuking Him.
8.33: But He, having turned back and having seen His disciples, rebuked Peter, saying, " Be going away behind Me, Satan! For you do not keep in mind the [ things ] of God, 9 but 9 the [ things ] of people. "

8.36: " For what will it benefit a person if he gains the whole world and forfeits his soul?

6.1: Now it happened on the second - first Sabbath [ fig., the first Sabbath of the second month ] He [ was ] passing through the grainfields, and His disciples were picking the heads of grain and were eating, rubbing [ the husk from the grain ] with their hands.

6.22: " Happy are you * when people hate you *, and when they exclude you * and insult [ or, denounce ] [ you * ] and cast out [ fig., scorn ] your * name as evil because of the Son of Humanity.

6.43: " For a good tree does not produce rotten fruit, nor does a rotten tree produce good fruit.

6.46: " And why do you * call Me, 'Lord, Lord, ' and do not do what I say?

6.48: he is like a person building a house, who dug and went deep and laid a foundation on the solid rock, but a flood having come, the stream burst upon that house and was not able to shake it, for it had been founded on the solid rock.

7.1: Now when He completed all His sayings in the ears of the people, He entered into Capernaum.

7.26: " 9 But 9 what have you * gone out to see? A prophet? Yes, I say to you *, and much more [ than ] a prophet.
7.27: " This is [ he ] concerning whom it has been written, " Look! 9 I 9 am sending My messenger before Your face [ fig., ahead of You ], who will prepare Your way before You. " [ Mal 3: 1 ]

7.29: And all the people having heard, and the tax collectors, they justified God [ or, acknowledged God's righteousness ], having been baptized with the baptism of John.
7.30: But the Pharisees and the lawyers rejected the counsel [ or, purpose ] of God for themselves, not having been baptized by him.
7.31: " To what then will I compare the people of this generation? And to what are they similar to?
7.32: " They are similar to young children, the ones sitting in a market - place and calling to one another and saying, 'We played a flute for you *, and you * did not dance; we mourned for you *, and you * did not weep! '

7.42: " But when they did not have [ anything ] to pay back, he freely forgave both. So tell [ Me ], which of them will love him more? "
7.43: Then answering, Simon said, " I suppose that [ it is the one ] to whom he freely forgave the greater [ amount ]. " And He said to him, " You judged correctly. "
7.44: And having turned to the woman, He said to Simon, " See this woman? I entered into your house; you did not give water for My feet, but this [ woman ] wet My feet with her tears and wiped [ them ] dry with the hairs of her head.
7.45: " You did not give a kiss to Me, but this [ woman ], from what [ time ] [ fig., since ] I came in [ has ] not stopped affectionately kissing my feet.

7.47: " For this reason, I say to you, her many sins have been forgiven, because she loved much. But [ the one ] to whom little is forgiven, loves little. "

8.33: Then the demons having gone out from the man, entered into the pigs, and the herd stampeded down the steep bank into the lake and were drowned.
8.34: Now the ones feeding [ the pigs ], having seen the [ thing ] having happened, fled and reported [ it ] in the city and in the fields.

12.50: " But I have a baptism to be baptized [ with ], and how distressed I am until it is completed!
12.51: " Do you * think that I came to give peace on the earth? Not at all, I say to you *, 9 but 9 rather division!

12.53: " A father will be divided against a son and a son against a father, a mother against a daughter and a daughter against a mother, a mother - in - law against her daughter - in - law and a daughter - in - law against her mother - in - law. " [ see Micah 7: 6 ]

13.22: And He was passing through according to [ fig., through various ] cities and villages teaching and making a journey to Jerusalem.
13.23: Now someone said to Him, " Lord, are the ones being saved few? " And He said to them,

14.1: And it happened, when He went into [ the ] house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, that 9 they 9 were watching Him closely.

14.14: and you will be happy [ or, blessed ], because they do not have [ anything ] to repay to you, for it will be repaid to you in the resurrection of the righteous. "
14.15: Then one of the ones reclining [ to eat ] with [ Him ], having heard these things, said to him, " Happy [ or, Blessed ] [ is he ] who will eat dinner in the kingdom of God. "
14.16: But He said to him, " A certain man prepared a great banquet, and he invited many;
14.17: and he sent his slave at the hour of the banquet to say to the ones having been invited, 'Be coming, because all [ things ] are now ready. '

16.1: Now He was also saying to His disciples, " A certain man was rich, who had a steward, and this [ steward ] was accused to him as squandering his possessions.

17.21: neither will they say, 'Look here! ' or 'Look there! ' For listen! The kingdom of God is within [ or, among ] you *. "
17.22: Then He said to His disciples, " Days will come when you * will long to see one of the days of the Son of Humanity, and you * will not see [ it ].

17.28: " Likewise also, as it happened in the days of Lot: they were eating, they were drinking, they were buying, they were selling, they were planting, [ and ] they were building;
17.29: but [ on the ] day which Lot went out from Sodom, He rained fire and sulfur [ or, brimstone ] from heaven and destroyed [ them ] all.
17.30: " According to these [ things ] [ fig., In the same way ] it will be in [ the ] day which the Son of Humanity is revealed.
17.31: " In that day, [ the one ] who will be on the house top and his goods in the house, he must not come down to take them away. And the [ one ] in the field, likewise, he must not turn back for the [ things left ] behind.
17.32: " Be remembering the wife of Lot!
17.33: " Whoever seeks to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses it will preserve it.

18.4: " And he did not wantI [ to ] for a time, but after these [ things ] he said in himself, 'Even though I do not fear God and do not respect humanity,

3.13: " And no one has ascended into heaven, except the One having descended from heaven - the Son of Humanity, the One being in heaven.

3.19: " Now this is the judgment, that the Light has come into the world, and people loved the darkness rather than the Light, for their works were evil.
3.20: " For every [ one ] practicing wicked [ things ] hates the Light and does not come towards the Light, so that his works shall not be exposed.

3.22: After these things Jesus and His disciples came into the land of Judea, and there He was staying with them and was baptizing.
3.23: But John was also baptizing in Aenon, near to Salem, because [ there ] was many waters [ or, much water ] in that place. And they were coming and were being baptized -
3.24: for John had not yet been cast into the prison.
3.25: Therefore, [ there ] occurred a dispute from the disciples of John with a Jew concerning purification [ rites ].
3.26: And they came to John and said to him, " Rabbi, [ He ] who was with you beyond the Jordan, to whom you have testified, look!, this One is baptizing, and all are coming to Him! "
3.27: John answered and said, " A person is not able to be receiving anything unless it has been given him from heaven.
3.28: " 9 You * 9 yourselves testify that I said, 'I myself am not the Christ', 9 but 9 'I have been sent before that One. '
3.29: " The one having the bride is [ the ] bridegroom, but the friend of the bridegroom, the one standing and hearing him, rejoices with joy because of the voice of the bridegroom. Therefore, [ in ] this my joy has been fulfilled.
3.30: " It is necessary [ for ] that One to be increasing, but [ for ] me to becoming less.
3.31: " The One coming from above is above all; the one being from the earth is from the earth and speaks from the earth; the One coming from heaven is above all.
3.32: " And what He has seen and heard, this He testifies, and no one receives His testimony.
3.33: " The one receiving His testimony [ has ] certified that God is true.
3.34: " For [ He ] whom God sent speaks the sayings of God, for God does not give the Spirit by measure.
3.35: " The Father loves the Son and has given all [ things ] into His hand.
3.36: " The one believing [ or, trusting ] in the Son has eternal life, but the one refusing to believe the Son will not see, 9 but 9 the wrath of God abides on him. "

4.1: So when the Lord knew that the Pharisees heard that Jesus is making and baptizing more disciples than John,
4.2: ( although Jesus Himself was not baptizing, 9 but 9 His disciples ),
4.3: He left Judea and went away into Galilee.
4.4: And it was necessary [ for ] Him to be passing through Samaria.
4.5: Then He comes to a city of Samaria, being called Sychar, near the place which Jacob gave to Joseph his son.
4.6: Now a well of Jacob was there. So Jesus, having grown weary from the journey, was sitting thus by the well. It was about the sixth hour [ i. e. 12: 00 noon Jewish time or 6: 00 p. m. Roman time ].
4.7: A woman comes from Samaria to draw water. Jesus says to her, " Give Me to drink. "
4.8: ( for His disciples had gone away into the city, so that they should buy food. )
4.9: So the Samaritan woman says to Him, " How is it that You, being a Jew, ask to drink from me, being a Samaritan woman? " ( for Jews do not associate with Samaritans ).
4.10: Jesus answered and said to her, " If you knew the free gift of God and who is the One saying to you, 'Give Me to drink, ' you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water. "
4.11: The woman says to Him, " Lord, You do not even have a vessel to draw with, and the well is deep; from where then do You have this living water?
4.12: " 9 You 9 are not greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well, and [ he ] himself drank out of it, and his sons and his cattle, are You? "
4.13: Jesus answered and said to her, " Every [ one ] drinking of this water will thirst again.
4.14: " But whoever drinks of the water which 9 I 9 will give to him will by no means thirst into the age [ fig., ever thirst again ]! 9 But 9 the water which I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life! "
4.15: The woman says to Him, " Lord, give this water to me so that I shall not be thirsting nor coming to this place to be drawing. "
4.16: Jesus says to her, " Be going, call your husband and come to this place. "
4.17: The woman answered and said, " I do not have a husband. " Jesus says to her, " Correctly you said, 'I do not have a husband. '
4.18: " For five husbands you had, and [ the one ] whom you now have is not your husband; this you have said truly. "
4.19: The woman says to him, " Lord, I perceive that 9 You 9 are a prophet.
4.20: " Our fathers prostrated themselves in worship in this mountain, and 9 you * 9 say, 'In Jerusalem is the place where it is necessary to be prostrating in worship. ' "
4.21: Jesus says to her, " Woman, be believing Me, that an hour is coming when neither in this mountain nor in Jerusalem will you * prostrate yourselves in worship before the Father.
4.22: " 9 You * 9 prostrate yourselves in worship before what you * do not know; we prostrate ourselves in worship before what we know, because salvation is from the Jews.
4.23: " 9 But 9 an hour is coming and now is when the true worshipers will prostrate themselves in worship before the Father in spirit and truth, for indeed the Father is seeking such to be prostrating themselves in worship before Him.
4.24: " God [ is ] Spirit [ or, [ is ] as to His essence Spirit ], and it is necessary [ for ] the ones prostrating themselves in worship before Him to be prostrating in worship in spirit and truth. "
4.25: The woman says to Him, " I know that Messiah is coming, the one being called Christ, when that One comes He will tell us all things. "
4.26: Jesus says to her, " 9 I 9 am, the One speaking to you. "
4.27: And upon this [ or, at this [ point ] ] His disciples came, and they were marveling that He was speaking with a woman, although no one said, " What are You seeking? " or " Why are You speaking with her? "
4.28: Then the woman left her water - jug and went away into the city. And she says to the people,
4.29: " Come! See a Man who told me all [ things ] - as many as I did. This is not the Christ, is it? "
4.30: They went out from the city and were coming towards Him.
4.31: But in the meantime His disciples were asking Him, saying, " Rabbi, eat. "
4.32: But He said to them, " 9 I 9 have food to eat which you * do not know. "
4.33: So the disciples said to one another, " Someone has not brought Him [ something ] to eat, has he? "
4.34: Jesus says to them, " 9 My 9 food is that I should be doing the will of the One having sent Me and should finish His work.
4.35: " Do 9 you * 9 not say, 'It is yet four months and the harvest comes? ' Listen! 9 I 9 say to you *, lift up your * eyes and see the fields, that they are already white to harvest.
4.36: " And the one reaping receives a reward and gathers fruit to eternal life, so that both the one sowing and the one reaping shall rejoice together.
4.37: " For in this the word is true, 'One is the one sowing and another is the one reaping. ' " [ cp. Judges 6: 3, 4; Micah 6: 15 ]
4.38: " 9 I 9 sent you * to be reaping what 9 you * 9 have not labored [ for ]; others have labored, and 9 you * 9 have entered into their labor. "
4.39: Now from that city many of the Samaritans believed [ or, trusted ] in Him, because of the word of the woman testifying, " He told me all [ things ] - as many as I did. "
4.40: So when the Samaritans came to Him, they kept asking Him to remain with them, and He remained there two days.
4.41: And many more believed because of His word.
4.42: And so they were saying to the woman, " No longer do we believe because of your speech, for we ourselves have heard and know that this is truly the Savior of the world - the Christ! "
4.43: But after the two days He went out from there and went away into Galilee.
4.44: For Jesus Himself testified that a prophet does not have honor in his hometown.
4.45: So when He came into Galilee, the Galileans received Him, having seen all [ things ] which He did in Jerusalem at the feast, for they also went to the feast.
4.46: So Jesus came again to Cana of Galilee, where He made the water wine. And [ there ] was a certain royal official whose son was sick in Capernaum.
4.47: This one, having heard that Jesus is coming out of Judea to Galilee, went away to Him and kept asking Him that He come down and heal his son, for he was about to die.
4.48: So Jesus said to him, " Unless you * see signs and wonders you * shall by no means believe. "
4.49: The royal official says to Him, " Lord, come down before my young child dies! "
4.50: Jesus says to him, " Be going; your son lives! " And the man believed [ or, trusted in ] the word which Jesus said to him and was going.
4.51: But already as he was going down, his slaves met him and reported, saying, " Your child lives! "
4.52: So he inquired of them the hour in which he got better. And they said to him, " Yesterday at the seventh hour [ i. e. 1: 00 p. m. Jewish time or 7: 00 p. m. Roman time ] the fever left him. "
4.53: Then the father knew that [ it was ] in that hour in which Jesus said to him, " Your son lives! " And he himself believed, and his whole house.
4.54: This again [ is the ] second sign Jesus did, having come out of Judea to Galilee.

5.1: After these things [ there ] was feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
5.2: Now [ there ] is in Jerusalem by the sheep - [ gate ] a pool, the one being called in Hebrew Bethesda, having five porticoes [ or, covered walkways ].
5.3: In these were lying a great multitude of ones being sick, blind, lame, [ and ] withered, waiting for the moving of the water.
5.4: For at a set time an angel would be descending into the pool and would be stirring up the water, then the first [ one ] having stepped in after the troubling of the water became well of whatever disease he was being held.
5.5: Now [ there ] was a certain man there having the infirmity thirty eight years.
5.6: Jesus having seen this one lying [ there ] and having known that a long time he had already [ been there ], He says to him, " Do you wish to become well? "
5.7: The one being sick answered Him, " Lord, I [ do ] not have a person that, whenever the water is stirred up, he should put me into the pool, but while 9 I 9 am coming another descends before me. "
5.8: Jesus says to him, " Get up! Take up your cot and be walking about. "
5.9: And immediately the man became well and took up his cot and began walking about! But it was a Sabbath on that day.
5.10: Therefore the Jews were saying to the one having been healed, " It is a Sabbath! It is not lawful for you to take up your cot. "
5.11: He answered them, " The One having made me well, that [ One ] said to me, 'Take up your cot and be walking about. ' "
5.12: So they questioned him, " Who is the Person, the One saying to you, 'Take up your cot and be walking about? ' "
5.13: But the one having been healed did not know who He is, for Jesus left unnoticed, a crowd being in that place.
5.14: After these things, Jesus finds him in the temple and said to him, " Look! You have become well! No longer be sinning, lest something worse should happen to you. "
5.15: The man went away and told the Jews that it is Jesus, the One making him well.
5.16: And for this reason the Jews were persecuting Jesus and were seeking to kill Him, because He was doing these things on a Sabbath.
5.17: But Jesus answered them, " My Father is working until now, and 9 I 9 am working. "
5.18: Therefore, for this reason, all the more the Jews were seeking to kill Him, because not only was He breaking the Sabbath, 9 but 9 He also called God His own Father, making Himself equal to God.
5.19: So Jesus answered and said to them, " Most positively, I say to you *, the Son is not able to be doing anything of Himself unless He sees the Father doing [ it ], for whatever He is doing, these also the Son likewise does.
5.20: " For the Father affectionately loves the Son and shows to Him all which He Himself does, and greater works than these He will show to Him, so that 9 you * 9 shall be marveling.
5.21: " For even as the Father raises the dead [ ones ] and makes alive, so also the Son makes alive whom He wills.
5.22: " For neither does the Father judge anyone, 9 but 9 He has given all judgment to the Son,
5.23: so that all shall be honoring the Son just as they honor the Father. The one not honoring the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him.
5.24: " Most positively, I say to you *, the one hearing My word and believing [ or, trusting ] the One having sent Me has eternal life and does not come into judgment, 9 but 9 has passed from death into life!
5.25: " Most positively, I say to you *, an hour is coming and now is when the dead [ ones ] will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those having heard will live.
5.26: " For even as the Father has life in Himself, so He gave also to the Son to be having life in Himself.
5.27: " And He gave also to Him authority to be making judgment, because He is [ the ] Son of Humanity.
5.28: " Stop marveling at this, because an hour is coming in which all those in the tombs will hear His voice,
5.29: and they will come forth: the ones having done the good [ things ] into a resurrection of life, but the ones having practiced the wicked [ things ] into a resurrection of judgment.
5.30: " 9 I 9 am not able to be doing anything of Myself. Just as I hear I judge, and My judgment is righteous, because I do not seek My will 9 but 9 the will of the Father having sent Me.
5.31: " If I testify concerning Myself, My testimony is not true.
5.32: " Another is the One testifying concerning Me, and I know that the testimony is true which He testifies concerning Me.
5.33: " You * have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.
5.34: " But 9 I 9 do not receive testimony from a man, 9 but 9 these things I say so that you * shall be saved.
5.35: " That one was the burning and shining lamp, but 9 you * 9 were pleased to be very glad for an hour [ or, for a while ] in his light.
5.36: " But 9 I 9 have the testimony greater than John's, for the works which the Father gave to Me that I should finish them, the works themselves which 9 I 9 am doing, they testify concerning Me that the Father has sent Me.
5.37: " And the Father having sent Me, [ He ] Himself has testified concerning Me. Neither have you * heard His voice at any time nor have you * seen His form.
5.38: And you * [ do ] not have His word remaining in you *, because whom that One sent, this One you * do not believe.
5.39: " You * search the Scriptures, because you * think in them to be having eternal life, and these they are which testify concerning Me.
5.40: " And you * are not willing to come to Me so that you * shall have life.
5.41: " I do not receive glory from people.
5.42: " 9 But 9 I have known you *, that you * do not have the love of God in yourselves.
5.43: " 9 I 9 have come in the Name of My Father, and you * do not receive Me. If another comes in his own name, that one you * will receive.
5.44: " How are 9 you * 9 able to believe, while receiving glory from one another, and the glory that [ is ] from God alone you * do not seek?
5.45: " Stop thinking that 9 I 9 will accuse you * before the Father; the one accusing you * is Moses, in whom you * have hoped [ or, have trusted in ].
5.46: " For if you * were believing Moses, you * would have been believing Me, for that one wrote concerning Me.
5.47: " But if the writings of that one you * do not believe, how will you * believe My sayings? "

6.1: After these things Jesus departed to the other side of the sea of Galilee ( that [ is ], of Tiberias ).
6.2: And a large crowd was following Him, because they were seeing His signs which He was doing upon the ones being sick.
6.3: But Jesus went up into the mountain, and He was sitting there with His disciples.
6.4: Now the Passover was near, the feast of the Jews.
6.5: Then Jesus, having lifted up His eyes and having seen that a large crowd is coming to Him, says to Philip, " From where shall we buy loaves of bread, so that these shall eat? "
6.6: ( But this He said testing him, for He Himself knew what He was about to be doing. )
6.7: Philip answered Him, " Two hundred denarii [ i. e., 200 days' wages ] [ worth ] of loaves of bread are not sufficient for them that each of them shall receive some little [ piece ]. "
6.8: One of His disciples, Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, says to Him,
6.9: " There is one little boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish, 9 but 9 these - what are they to so many? "
6.10: But Jesus said, " Make the people to recline. " Now there was much grass in the place. So they reclined ( the men in number about five thousand ).
6.11: Then Jesus took the loaves of bread, and having given thanks, He distributed to the disciples, and the disciples to the ones reclining, likewise also of the fish, as much as they wanted!
6.12: And when they were satisfied, He says to His disciples, " Gather together the broken pieces of bread having been leftover, so that nothing shall be lost. "
6.13: So they gathered together and filled twelve hand - baskets with broken pieces of bread from the five barley loaves which were left over by the ones having eaten.
6.14: Therefore, the people having seen the sign Jesus did, said, " This is truly the Prophet, the One coming into the world! "
6.15: Then Jesus, having known that they are about to come and to take Him by force so that they should make Him king, withdrew into the mountain Himself alone.
6.16: But when evening came, His disciples went down to the sea.
6.17: And having stepped into the boat, they began going over the sea to Capernaum. And it had already become dark, and Jesus had not come to them.
6.18: And the sea was being stirred up by a strong blowing wind.
6.19: Then having rowed about twenty - five or thirty stadia [ about three or four miles or five or six kilometers ], they watched Jesus walking about on the sea and coming near the boat. And they were afraid.
6.20: But He says to them, " 9 I 9 am! Stop being afraid! "
6.21: So they were willing to receive Him into the boat, and immediately the boat came to be on the land to which they were going.
6.22: The next day, the crowd which was standing on the other side of the sea, having seen that [ there ] was no other small boat there except that one which His disciples stepped into, and that Jesus did not enter with His disciples into the little boat, 9 but 9 His disciples went away alone.
6.23: ( But other small boats came from Tiberias, near the place where they ate the bread, the Lord having given thanks ).
6.24: So when the crowd saw that Jesus is not there, nor His disciples, they themselves stepped into the boats and came to Capernaum seeking Jesus.
6.25: And having found Him on the other side of the sea, they said to Him, " Rabbi, when have You come here? "
6.26: Jesus answered them and said, " Most positively, I say to you *, you * seek Me, not because you * saw signs, 9 but 9 because you * ate of the loaves of bread and were satisfied.
6.27: " Stop working [ for ] the food that perishes by itself, 9 but 9 [ be working for ] the food that remains to eternal life, which the Son of Humanity will give to you *, for God the Father has set [ His ] seal [ on ] Him. "
6.28: Therefore, they said to Him, " What shall we be doing so that we shall be working the works of God? "
6.29: Jesus answered and said to them, " This is the work of God, that you * be believing [ or, trusting ] in Him whom that One sent. "
6.30: So they said to Him, " What sign then do You do so that we shall see and believe You? What are You working?
6.31: " Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, just as it has been written, 'He gave to them bread out of heaven to eat. ' " [ Exod 16: 4; Neh #: 15; Ps 78: 24 ]
6.32: So Jesus said to them, " Most positively, I say to you *, Moses has not given to you * the bread out of heaven, 9 but 9 My Father gives to you * the true bread out of heaven.
6.33: " For the bread of God is the One coming down out of heaven and giving life to the world. "
6.34: Then they said to Him, " Lord, always give to us this bread. "
6.35: But Jesus said to them, " 9 I 9 am the bread of life! The one coming to Me shall by no means hunger, and the one believing [ or, trusting ] in Me will by no means thirst at any time!
6.36: " 9 But 9 I said to you * that you * have both seen Me and you * do not believe.
6.37: " All that the Father gives to Me will come to Me, and the one coming to Me I shall by no means cast out.
6.38: " Because I have come down out of heaven, not so that I shall be doing My will, 9 but 9 the will of the One having sent Me.
6.39: " And this is the will of the Father having sent Me, that out of all which He has given to Me I will not lose [ any of ] it, 9 but 9 I will raise it up the last day.
6.40: " And this is the will of the One having sent me, that every [ one ] looking on the Son and believing [ or, trusting ] in Him shall be having eternal life, and 9 I 9 will raise him up on the last day. "
6.41: Therefore, the Jews were grumbling about Him, because He said, " 9 I 9 am the bread having come down out of heaven. "
6.42: And they said, " Is this not Jesus, the Son of Joseph, whose father and mother 9 we 9 know? How then says this One, " I have come down out of heaven? "
6.43: So Jesus answered and said to them, " Stop grumbling with one another.
6.44: " No one is able to come to Me unless the Father having sent Me draws [ or, drags ] him, and 9 I 9 will raise him up in the last day.
6.45: " It has been written in the prophets, 'And they will all be taught of God. ' Therefore, every [ one ] hearing from the Father and having learned comes to Me. [ Isaiah 54: 13 ]
6.46: " Not that anyone has seen the Father, except the One being from God, He has seen the Father.
6.47: " Most positively, I say to you *, the one believing in Me has eternal life.
6.48: " 9 I 9 am the bread of life!
6.49: " Your * fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, and they died.
6.50: " This is the bread which comes down out of heaven, so that anyone shall eat from it and shall not die.
6.51: " 9 I 9 am the living bread, the One having come down from heaven. If anyone eats from this bread he will live into the age [ fig., forever ], and indeed the bread which 9 I 9 will give is My flesh, which I will give on behalf of the life of the world. "
6.52: Therefore, the Jews began disputing with one another, saying, " How is this One able to give to us His flesh to eat? "
6.53: So Jesus said to them, " Most positively, I say to you *, unless you * eat the flesh of the Son of Humanity and drink His blood, you * do not have life in yourselves.
6.54: " The one eating My flesh and drinking My blood has eternal life, and 9 I 9 will raise him up the last day.
6.55: " For My flesh truly is food, and My blood truly is drink.
6.56: " The one eating My flesh and drinking My blood remains in Me, and I in him.
6.57: " Just as the living Father sent Me, and I live because of the Father, also the one feeding on Me, that one will also live because of Me.
6.58: " This is the bread having come down out of heaven, not as your * fathers ate the manna and died. The one eating this bread will live into the age [ fig., forever ]! "
6.59: These things He said in a synagogue, teaching in Capernaum.
6.60: Therefore, many having heard from His disciples, said, " This word is harsh. Who is able to be hearing it? "
6.61: But Jesus, knowing in Himself that His disciples are grumbling about this, said to them, " Does this cause you * to stumble [ fig, offend you * ]?
6.62: " Then [ what ] if you * shall be watching the Son of Humanity ascending where He was before?
6.63: " The Spirit is the One giving life; the flesh does not accomplish [ or, benefit ] anything. The words which 9 I 9 have spoken to you * are spirit and are life!
6.64: " 9 But 9 there are some of you * who do not believe. " For Jesus knew from [ the ] beginning who they are, the ones not believing, and who is the one [ who ] will be betraying Him.
6.65: And He said, " For this reason I have said to you *, 'No one is able to come to Me unless it has been given to him from My Father. ' "
6.66: From this [ time ] many went away of His disciples to the things behind and were no more walking about with Him.
6.67: So Jesus said to the twelve, " 9 You * 9 do not also want to be going away, do you *? "
6.68: Then Simon Peter answered Him, " Lord, to whom will we go? You have [ the ] words of eternal life. "
6.69: " And we have come to believe and have come to know that 9 You 9 are the Christ, the Son of the living God! "
6.70: Jesus answered them, " 9 I 9 chose you *, the twelve, did I not? And one of you * is a devil! "
6.71: Now He spoke of Judas Iscariot, [ son ] of Simon, for this one was about to be betraying Him, being one of the twelve.

7.1: And Jesus was walking about after these things in Galilee, for He was not wanting to be walking in Judea because the Jews were seeking to kill Him.
7.2: But the feast of the Jews was near, the Feast of Tabernacles.
7.3: So His brothers said to Him, " Depart from here and be going into Judea, so that Your disciples also will watch Your works which You are doing.
7.4: " For no one does anything in secret and himself seeks to be in public. If You do these things, show Yourself to the world. "
7.5: For His brothers were not believing in Him.
7.6: So Jesus says to them, " My time is not yet present; but your time is always ready.
7.7: " The world is not able to be hating you *, but Me it hates because 9 I 9 testify concerning it that its works are evil.
7.8: " 9 You * 9 go up to this feast; 9 I 9 am not yet going up to this feast because My time has not yet been fulfilled. "
7.9: And having said these things to them, He remained in Galilee.
7.10: But when His brothers went up, then also He Himself went up to the feast, not openly, 9 but 9 as in secret.
7.11: So the Jews were seeking Him at the feast and said, " Where is that One? "
7.12: And there was much grumbling [ or, whispering ] concerning Him among the crowds. Some indeed said, " He is good. " Others said, " No, 9 but 9 He is leading the crowd astray [ fig., deceiving the crowd ]. "

7.14: But now in the middle of the feast Jesus went up into the temple and began teaching.
7.15: And the Jews were marveling, saying, " How does this One know letters, not having learned? " [ or, How is this One learned, not having been educated? ]
7.16: Therefore, Jesus answered them and said, " My teaching is not mine, 9 but 9 of the One having sent Me.
7.17: " If anyone is willing to be doing His will, he will know concerning such teaching, whether it is from God or [ whether ] 9 I 9 speak from Myself.
7.18: " The one speaking from himself seeks his own glory, but the One seeking the glory of the One having sent Him, this One is true, and unrighteousness is not in Him.
7.19: " Has not Moses given to you * the Law? And not one of you * does the Law. Why are you * seeking to kill Me? "
7.20: The crowd answered and said, " You have a demon! Who seeks to kill You? "
7.21: Jesus answered and said to them, " One work I did, and you * all marvel [ or, are amazed ]!
7.22: " For this reason Moses has given to you * circumcision - not that it is from Moses, 9 but 9 from the fathers - and on a Sabbath you * circumcise a man.
7.23: " If a man receives circumcision on a Sabbath so that the Law of Moses is not broken, [ why ] are you * very angry with Me that I made a man entirely well on a Sabbath?

7.48: " 9 But 9 the Most High does not dwell in temples made with human hands, just as the prophet says,
7.49: 'Heaven [ is ] My throne, but the earth [ is ] a footstool for My feet. What kind of house will you * build for Me? ' says the LORD, 'Or what [ is ] My place of rest? '

8.1: Now Saul was giving approval to his murder. Then in that day a great persecution took place on the assembly, the one in Jerusalem, and all were scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.

8.30: So Philip having run up, heard him reading aloud the prophet Isaiah, and he said, " So do you understand what you are reading? "
8.31: Then he said, " For how could I unless someone guides me? " And he invited Philip, having come up, to sit with him.
8.32: Now the passage of the Scripture which he was reading aloud was this: " He was led as a sheep to slaughter, and as a lamb before the one shearing it [ is ] silent, so He does not open His mouth.
8.33: " In His humiliation his justice was taken away, but who will describe His generation? Because His life is taken away from the earth. " [ Isaiah 53: 7, 8 ]
8.34: So answering, the eunuch said to Philip, " I ask you, about whom does the prophet say this? About himself or about some other [ person ]? "
8.35: Then Philip, having opened his mouth and having begun from this Scripture, proclaimed the Gospel [ about ] Jesus to him.
8.36: Now as they were traveling down the road, they came upon some water. And the eunuch said, " Look! Water! What prevents me [ from being ] baptized? "
8.38: And he commanded the chariot to stand still. And they both went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.
8.39: Now when they came up out of the water, [ the ] Spirit of the Lord caught Philip up, and the eunuch no longer saw him, for he began going his way rejoicing.

9.1: Now Saul, still breathing threat [ s ] and murder against the disciples of the Lord, having gone to the high priest,

9.6: " 9 But 9 get up and enter into the city, and it will be told to you what it is necessary [ for ] you to be doing. "

9.29: and he was speaking and disputing with the Greek - speaking Jews. But they were attempting to execute him,

9.35: And all the ones living [ in ] Lydda and Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.
9.36: Now in Joppa [ there ] was a certain female disciple, by name Tabitha, ( which, being translated, is being called Dorcas ); this [ woman ] was full of good works and charitable giving which she was doing.
9.37: Then it happened in those days, having been sick, she died. So having washed her [ body ], they laid her in an upstairs room.
9.38: Now Lydda being close to Joppa, the disciples having heard that Peter is in it [ i. e. Lydda ], sent [ messengers ] to him urging [ him ] not to delay to come over to them.
9.39: So Peter having gotten up, went with them, whom having arrived, they brought [ him ] into the upstairs room. And all the widows stood by him weeping and showing tunics and cloaks, as many as Dorcas used to make while being with them.
9.40: But Peter having sent them all outside, having placed the knees [ fig., having knelt down ], prayed; and having turned to the body, he said, " Tabitha, get up! " Then she opened her eyes, and having seen Peter, she sat up!
9.41: Then having given her [ his ] hand, he lifted her up; and having called the holy ones and the widows, he presented her living.
9.42: Now it became known throughout all of Joppa, and many believed on the Lord.
9.43: And it happened, [ that ] he stayed many days in Joppa, with a certain Simon a tanner [ i. e. a person who converts animal hides into leather ].

10.1: Now [ there ] was a certain man in Caesarea, by name Cornelius, a centurion of a garrison [ of soldiers ], the one being called Italian [ fig., a captain of the Italian Regiment ],
10.2: devout and fearing God [ i. e. a worshipper of the one true God, but not a full convert to Judaism, also called " God - worshiping " ] together with all his house, and doing [ or, giving ] many charitable gifts to the people and imploring God through all [ fig. continually ].

10.4: Then having looked intently at him and having become terrified, he said, " What is it, Lord? " So he said to him, " Your prayers and your charitable gifts [ have ] ascended as a memorial before God.
10.5: " And now send men to Joppa and summon Simon, the one being called Peter.
10.6: " This [ man ] is staying as a guest with a certain Simon a tanner, whose house is by [ the ] sea. "
10.7: So when the angel, the one speaking to Cornelius, left, having summoned two of his household servants and a devout soldier [ from among ] the ones waiting on him continually,
10.8: and having explained everything to them, he sent them to Joppa.
10.9: Now the next day, as these are traveling and approaching the city, Peter went up on the housetop to pray, about [ the ] sixth hour [ i. e. 12: 00 noon ].
10.10: But he became very hungry and was desiring to eat; but while they [ were ] preparing [ a meal ], a trance fell on him,
10.11: and he observes heaven [ or, the sky ] having been opened, and a certain object like a great sheet descending to him, having been tied at [ the ] four corners and being lowered on the ground,
10.12: in which were all the four - footed animals of the earth and the wild beasts and the reptiles and the birds of heaven [ or, the air ].
10.13: And a voice came to him: " Having gotten up, Peter, slaughter and eat! "
10.14: But Peter said, " Most certainly not, Lord! Because never did I eat any [ thing ] common [ fig., ritually impure ] or unclean [ or, which defiles ]. "
10.15: And a voice [ came ] again a second time to him: " What God [ has ] cleansed, by all means stop calling common [ fig., ritually impure ]! "
10.16: Now this was done three times, and again the object was taken up into heaven.
10.17: Now as Peter was thoroughly perplexed in himself what the vision which he saw might be [ fig., mean ], then look!, the men, the ones having been sent from Cornelius, having found by inquiry the house of Simon, stood at the gate.
10.18: And having called, they were asking whether Simon, the one being called Peter, is staying here as a guest.
10.19: Now as Peter [ was ] pondering about the vision, the Spirit said to him, " Listen! Men are seeking you.
10.20: " 9 But 9 having gotten up, go down and go with them, doubting nothing [ fig., without hesitation ], because 9 I 9 have sent them. "
10.21: So Peter having gone down to the men, said, " Listen! 9 I 9 am [ the one ] whom you * are seeking. What [ is ] the reason for which you * are here? "
10.22: Then they said, " Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous man and fearing God, and well spoken of by [ the ] whole nation of the Jews, was divinely directed by a holy angel to summon you to his house and to hear words from you. "
10.23: So having invited them in, he received [ them ] as guests. Then the next day Peter went away with them, and some of the brothers from Joppa went with him.
10.24: And the next day they entered into Caesarea. Now Cornelius was waiting for them, having called together his relatives and close friends.
10.25: Then when it happened [ that ] Peter entered, Cornelius having met him, having fallen at [ his ] feet, prostrated himself in worship before [ him ].
10.26: But Peter raised him up, saying, " Stand up! 9 I 9 myself am also a person. "
10.27: And talking with him, he went in and finds many [ people ] having gathered.
10.28: And he said to them, " 9 You * 9 know how it is unlawful for a man, a Jew, to be associating with or to be visiting one of another race, and [ yet ] God showed to me to be calling no one common or unclean [ or, defiled ].

10.30: And Cornelius said, " From [ the ] fourth day [ fig., Four days ago ], I was fasting until this hour, and [ at ] the ninth hour [ i. e. 3: 00 p. m. ] praying in my house. And listen! A man stood before me in a shining robe!
10.31: " And he said, 'Cornelius, your prayer was heard and your charitable gifts are remembered before God.
10.32: 'Therefore, send [ men ] to Joppa and summon Simon, who is called Peter. This [ man ] is staying as a guest in [ the ] house of Simon, a tanner by the sea, who having arrived, will speak to you. '
10.33: " So I sent for you at once, and 9 you 9 did well, having arrived. Now then, 9 we 9 all are present before God to hear all the [ things ] having been commanded to you by God. "
10.34: Then Peter having opened his mouth, said, " Truly, I comprehend that God is not One to accept faces [ fig., to be prejudice ],
10.35: 9 but 9 in every nation the one fearing Him and working righteousness is acceptable to Him.
10.36: " The word which He sent to the sons [ and daughters ] of Israel, proclaiming the Gospel of peace through Jesus Christ - this One is Lord of all -
10.37: [ that word ] 9 you * 9 know, the word having taken place throughout the whole of Judea, having begun from Galilee, after the baptism which John preached -
10.38: Jesus who [ is ] from Nazareth - how God anointed Him with the [ the ] Holy Spirit and power, who went about doing good and healing all the ones being oppressed by the Devil, because God was with Him.
10.39: " And 9 we 9 are witnesses of all [ things ] which He did, both in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem; whom they also executed, having hanged [ Him ] on a tree [ or, cross ].

10.41: not to all the people, 9 but 9 to witnesses, the ones having been chosen beforehand by God, to us who ate together and drank together with Him after He rose from [ the ] dead.
10.42: " And He gave strict orders to us to preach to the people and to solemnly testify that He is the One having been designated by God [ to be ] Judge of living [ ones ] and dead [ ones ].
10.43: " To this One all the prophets bear witness [ that ] through His name every [ one ] that is believing [ or, trusting ] in Him receives forgiveness of sins. "
10.44: While Peter [ was ] still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all the ones hearing the word.
10.45: And the believing ones from the circumcision were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because the free gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out on the Gentiles also.
10.46: For they were hearing them speaking with tongues [ fig., other languages ] and magnifying God. Then Peter answered,
10.47: " Surely no one is able to forbid the water, can he, [ for ] these not to be baptized who received the Holy Spirit just as we also [ did ]? "
10.48: And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Then they urgently asked him to stay several days.

11.1: Now the apostles and the brothers [ and sisters ], the ones being throughout Judea, heard that the Gentiles also [ had ] received the word of God.

11.3: saying, " To men having foreskin [ fig., who are uncircumcised ] you went in and ate with them! "

11.28: Then one of them, by name Agabus, having stood up, signified [ or, foretold ] by the Spirit [ of ] a great famine being to happen over all the inhabited earth - which also [ or, then ] occurred during [ the reign of ] Claudius Caesar.
11.29: Then the disciples, just as anyone was prospering, each of them determined to send [ a contribution ] for ministry [ fig., relief ] to the brothers [ and sisters ] dwelling in Judea,
11.30: which they also did, having sent to the elders by [ the ] hand of Barnabas and Saul.
